item.title: 'Nobody else settled wars': Trump reasserts role in India-Pakistan ceasefire; makes renewed push for Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: US President Donald Trump, speaking during a White House meeting with oil executives on Venezuela, again claimed he stopped a looming India–Pakistan war, saying “eight planes were shot down” before he intervened. He argued that his role in resolving multiple conflicts, including between the nuclear-armed neighbours, made him deserving of a Nobel Peace Prize, repeating assertions he has made in earlier interviews.

item.title: Denied job over travel, wheelchair user went on to visit 55 countries across 7 continents
item.description: Cory Lee, a wheelchair user with spinal muscular atrophy, has turned a lifetime of barriers into a mission to travel the world. After being told his disability made travel impossible, he founded Curb Free With Cory Lee, visiting 55 countries across all seven continents while documenting accessibility, challenging assumptions, and reshaping what inclusive travel can look like.

item.title: Who is Lifeismizzy? Kick streamer goes viral after fake ticket prank turns tense and stranger issues threat on livestream
item.description: Marissa “Lifeismizzy” Gill went viral after a fake ticket prank on Kick turned tense when a man threatened her during a live stream. The clip spread online and raised interest in her content. At the same time, Kick streamer Braden “Clavicular” Peters returned after a ban linked to a Cybertruck incident, with TMZ reporting no charges.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Extreme asymmetry: Doctors warn after influencer spends 300 days training only one shoulder
item.description: A man known as “The Crooked Man” has spent more than 300 days training only one trapezius muscle to deliberately reject TikTok’s “looksmaxxing” trend. His extreme, asymmetrical transformation has gone viral online, but doctors warn the experiment could cause serious long-term musculoskeletal problems, outweighing any short-term strength gains or internet attention, and prompting debate about health, balance, and body image.

item.title: ‘Have cancelled’: Trump says no second strikes on Venezuela; pledges $100 billion investment
item.description: President Trump announced the cancellation of a "second wave of attacks" on Venezuela, citing the release of political prisoners and cooperation on rebuilding oil and gas infrastructure. He stated that "BIG OIL" will invest at least $100 billion, with meetings planned at the White House.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iran unrest: Tehran accuses US and Israel of stoking protests
item.description: Iran's foreign minister accused the US and Israel of fueling ongoing protests, while downplaying the likelihood of foreign military intervention. The demonstrations, sparked by economic woes, have seen a harsh crackdown, with authorities labeling protesters as 'terrorists' and imposing an internet blackout. US President Trump has warned Iran against suppressing demonstrators.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: President’s priority: Trump picks up Fox News call during New York Times interview
item.description: President Donald Trump took a call from Fox News during a New York Times interview. The interview, held in the Oval Office, was interrupted multiple times by phone calls. Trump also spoke with Colombian leader Gustavo Petro. This marked a rare extended engagement with the Times, a publication Trump has often criticized.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iran protests: Why are women lighting cigarettes from burning Khamenei photo? See photos
item.description: Iranian women are seen burning images of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei amidst escalating protests fueled by severe economic hardship. The nation's currency has plummeted, inflation has soared, and food prices have surged, leading to widespread discontent and demonstrations not seen since the 2022-23 unrest.

item.title: Switzerland holds memorial service during day of national mourning for bar fire victims
item.description: Switzerland mourned 40 lives lost in a New Year's Eve bar fire, a tragedy investigators believe was sparked by Champagne candles near the ceiling. Serious questions are being raised about fire safety compliance and inspections. Criminal investigations are underway for bar managers, with Italy and France also launching probes into the blaze that claimed several of their citizens.

item.title: ‘I got no credit, I was criticised’: Trump says he won’t keep business interests aside
item.description: President Donald Trump stated he won't restrict his family's business dealings in a potential second term, citing a lack of recognition for voluntary ethical restraints during his first presidency. He believes past efforts to distance his administration from his global business interests yielded only criticism, not credit. Trump feels these actions were unappreciated, shaping his current, more permissive stance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bangladesh unrest: British MP says attack on Hindus ‘very concerning’; urges UK to act
item.description: Former British home secretary Priti Patel has urged the UK government to use its diplomatic influence to address religious violence and persecution against Hindus in Bangladesh. Citing recent killings and unacceptable levels of violence, she has sought details on UK government actions and assurances from Bangladeshi authorities regarding minority protection.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Owning the sea': Moment US forces intercepted sanctioned oil tanker in Caribbean Sea - watch
item.description: The United States has seized a sanctioned oil tanker, the Olina, in international waters as part of an ongoing campaign against "ghost fleet" vessels. This action, aimed at enforcing sanctions on Venezuela's oil, has drawn strong condemnation from Moscow, which accuses the US of violating international law and risking escalation.

item.title: Thailand–Cambodia border truce: US announces $45mn aid package to stabilise ceasefire
item.description: The United States announced a $45 million aid package for Thailand and Cambodia to bolster a fragile border ceasefire and promote regional stability. The funds will support border communities, demining efforts, and programs to combat drug trafficking and online scams, reinforcing US commitment to a secure Indo-Pacific.
